items.markdown:
Thailand is generally safe for tourists , but `official advisories warn against all but essential travel to specific southern border provinces and parts of the Cambodian border` . You can review full updates directly on the [UK Foreign Travel Advice for Thailand](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/thailand) or the [US State Department Thailand Information Page](https://travel.state.gov/content/travel/en/international-travel/International-Travel-Country-Information-Pages/Thailand.html).[[1]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DV8DichEuG2/?hl=en)[[2]](https://www.andamandaphuket.com/blog/is-thailand-safe-to-travel)[[3]](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/thailand)[[4]](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/travel/advice/safe-to-travel-to-thailand-and-cambodia-latest-advice-fcdo/)[[5]](https://www.traveltalktours.com/thailand-travel-advice/)

Restricted and High-Risk Border Zones

- **Southern Provinces:** Avoid all but essential travel to Pattani, Yala, Narathiwat, and the southern Songkhla areas (including the Hat Yai-Padang Besar train line) due to regular localized violence.[](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/thailand) 
- **Cambodian Border:** Exercise heightened caution or avoid areas near the land border with Cambodia due to past military clashes, landmines, and suspended border crossings.[](https://www.gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/thailand) 

Entry Requirements and Health

- **Digital Arrival Card:** All non-Thai nationals must complete the mandatory Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC) online within 72 hours prior to arrival.[](https://www.ireland.ie/en/dfa/overseas-travel/advice/thailand/) [[1]](https://www.ireland.ie/en/dfa/overseas-travel/advice/thailand/)[[2]](https://tvc.co.th/guides/thailand-travel-advisory)
- **Health Precautions:** Tap water is unsafe to drink. Routine vaccinations and protection against mosquito-borne illnesses like dengue fever are strongly recommended.[](https://www.responsibletravel.com/holidays/thailand/travel-guide/thailand-travel-advice) [[1]](https://www.responsibletravel.com/holidays/thailand/travel-guide/thailand-travel-advice)

General Safety Tips

- **Major Hubs:** Popular tourist destinations such as Bangkok, Chiang Mai, Phuket, and Pattaya operate normally with standard safety conditions.
- **Emergency Contacts:** Save key numbers including the Tourist Police at **1155** and general emergency services at **191**.[](https://tvc.co.th/guides/thailand-travel-advisory) [[1]](https://www.facebook.com/nbtworld/posts/the-tourism-authority-of-thailand-tat-confirms-that-travel-and-tourism-activitie/1262661379231323/)

references.title: The Tourism Authority of Thailand (TAT) confirms that travel and tourism activities across Thailand are operating normally and remain unaffected. At the same time, TAT has issued a travel advisory stating that security measures have been increased in seven provinces along the Thailand–Cambodia border: Ubon Ratchathani, Si Sa Ket, Surin, Buri Ram, Sa Kaeo, Chanthaburi, and Trat. Martial law is in effect in Mueang Chanthaburi, Tha Mai, Makham, Laem Sing, Kaeng Hang Maew, Na Yai Am, and Khao Khitchakut districts of Chanthaburi; in Khok Sung, Ta Phraya, Aranyaprathet, and Khlong Hat districts of Sa Kaeo; and in Khlong Yai, Bo Rai, Laem Ngop, Khao Saming, and Mueang Trat districts of Trat. In addition, curfew measures are in place in four districts of Sa Kaeo, effective 10 December 2025, and in five districts of Trat, effective 14 December 2025, both in effect until further notice, restricting movement between 7 P.M. and 5 A.M. Despite these measures, domestic and international transport services, including air, rail, bus, and marine, continue to operate as usual.
